one_line: Pallava king of Kanchipuram who captured Vatapi in the long Pallava–Chalukya struggle, c. 7th century CE.

appearance.age_look: late 20s, athletic and wiry, with the confident bearing of a seasoned but still youthful ruler-warrior
appearance.face: oval face with sharp jawline, medium-brown South Indian complexion, straight nose, expressive dark eyes, a thin neatly trimmed moustache, and a calm, determined default expression that turns intense in battle scenes
appearance.hair: thick black hair drawn into a high, rounded topknot at the crown wrapped with a narrow gold band, sides smoothed back, a few short strands loose at the temples, no helmet but a simple golden forehead ornament centered above the brows
appearance.costume: He wears a knee-length off-white cotton tunic with short sleeves and a slightly flared hem, over which is a fitted reddish-brown leather chest harness holding his sword scabbard; a deep maroon silk dhoti with fine mustard-yellow border is wrapped tightly at the waist and pleated to fall to the ankles, paired with a narrow gold cloth belt knotted at the left hip; his upper torso and shoulders are modestly covered by a light saffron-colored cotton angavastra draped from the left shoulder across the chest and back; jewelry is era-accurate Pallava royal style but kept practical—simple broad gold armlets on both upper arms, a pair of medium-sized gold disc earrings, and a single short gold necklace with a central round pendant; he wears sturdy dark brown leather sandals with thong straps and a small round wooden tilaka-box tied at his waist by a thin cord, hinting at ritual preparation before battle.
appearance.signature: A slightly curved South Indian iron sword with a plain steel blade, a short wooden grip wrapped in dark leather, and a simple circular bronze guard, carried at his left hip in a dark brown leather scabbard that has a small carved lion-head motif near the mouth.

ref_desc: Narasimhavarman I appears as a medium-brown, oval-faced young warrior-king with a high black topknot and gold band, off-white tunic, maroon dhoti, saffron angavastra, modest gold ornaments, and a curved South Indian sword in a brown scabbard with lion motif.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Narasimhavarman I, a 7th-century Pallava warrior-king: an athletic, medium-brown South Indian man with an oval face, sharp jaw, thin moustache, and steady dark eyes, his thick black hair tied in a high rounded topknot wrapped by a narrow gold band and a simple golden forehead ornament above his brows. He wears an off-white knee-length cotton tunic with short sleeves, a fitted reddish-brown leather chest harness for his sword, and a deep maroon silk dhoti with fine mustard-yellow border wrapped tightly at the waist and pleated to the ankles. A light saffron cotton angavastra is draped from his left shoulder across his chest and back, covering the torso modestly. Show broad gold armlets on both upper arms, medium gold disc earrings, and a short gold necklace with a round central pendant. At his waist is a narrow gold cloth belt knotted at the left hip and a small round wooden tilaka-box tied by a thin cord. On his feet are sturdy dark brown leather sandals with thong straps. At his left hip hangs his signature weapon: a slightly curved South Indian iron sword with a plain steel blade, short leather-wrapped wooden grip, simple circular bronze guard, in a dark brown leather scabbard bearing a carved lion-head near the mouth. Emphasize the deep maroon, saffron, off-white, brown, and gold palette and show him from multiple angles to make the hairstyle, garments, and sword details clear.
